llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (cleaning OpenClaw session files) matches the files it touches, but the runtime instructions perform destructive file operations without safe-guards or clear selection criteria and could delete important session data if misapplied.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with the actions described in SKILL.md: listing, deleting old .jsonl session files and rebuilding sessions.json in ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/. No unrelated binaries, env vars, or installs are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct the agent to read and delete files under the user's home (~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/) and to rebuild sessions.json. However the guidance is vague about how to identify 'old cron sessions' and 'main session', provides no dry-run or backup steps, and does not require explicit user confirmation before deletion. That makes accidental data loss plausible.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only). This minimizes supply-chain risk because nothing is downloaded or written at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, or config paths beyond the session directory it manages; that is proportional to its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (good). However the skill can be invoked autonomously by the agent (default), and because it performs destructive file operations, autonomous invocation increases risk. The SKILL.md does not require explicit user approval before deletion.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill performs destructive cleanup of files under ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/ and rewrites sessions.json. Before installing or enabling it, insist on the following: 1) require the skill to perform a dry-run first that lists candidate files and shows the session.json changes, 2) require an explicit, user-confirmed approval step before any deletions, 3) create automatic backups of sessions.json and any files to be deleted (or export them to a backup folder) so you can restore if needed, 4) clarify the exact logic used to identify the 'main' session and which sessions are considered 'old cron' so you can audit it, and 5) avoid allowing autonomous runs without a confirmation toggle. If you cannot get these safeguards from the skill author, test the steps manually (or run the cleanup on a copy of your session directory) rather than letting the agent run it automatically.
llm.findings: [no_regex_findings] expected: This is an instruction-only skill with no code files, so the regex-based scanner had nothing to analyze; that is expected but means the SKILL.md is the primary security surface.
